t: This is Dover House, a Grade One listed mansion on Whitehall. Today it is the London headquarters of the Scotland Office, and it also houses the Office of the Advocate General for Scotland and the Independent Commission for Aid Impact. The architect James Paine, who also worked on Chatsworth, Thorndon Hall and Kedleston Hall, designed it. Sir Matthew Fetherstonhaugh, a politician and landowner, commissioned it. Henry Agar-Ellis, the fourth Viscount Clifden, was born in the house in 1863.
